title: Favorite trombonists and Kit Harris's band
summary: He names early trombone players, then Louie and George Nelson, who played with Kit Harris's band with George Williams and bassist Richard McLean.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Ask him who his favorite trombone players were in those days, way back.

He said, who was your favorite trombone player way back in those days? Who was the? Your favorite trombone player. Who was the best one? Yeah, your favorite. Oh, you know, I see. I left before I could play music good. It's, uh, let me see. Rob Palmer, did you say you know him? He's living there, you say? In Chicago.
In Chicago.

For him and then Duke. You know Duke? Zoo the Duke. Zoot? Yeah, trombone player. Yeah, yeah. Then set up a rule. Earl Humper. Harrison over the river, you know. And Yankee, he's there too. Yeah. And there's another trombone player over there. I said, this is man. Who did he play with? Kid Thomas. You know Kid Thomas? Yeah, you should play with him over there. Louie Nelson lives with him now. Louie Nelson? Huh? Louie Nelson? Louie Nelson? He's with Kid Thomas now. No, Louie Nelson was the clownette there. No, he's from— did you the clownette there? Tell them them. No. No. No. No.
No.
No.
No. No. No. No. No. No.

He said, this is Dr. Nelson's song. Oh, I used to play Louie Nelson and George Nelson. One played trampone and one played saxophone. Yeah, me and Louie, we used to play together a long time. It was Kit Harris then when we were playing together.
Who was Kit Harris?

He played just there. Kit Harris? Who was him? Huh? Kit Harris, I didn't know him. No, you didn't know Kit Harris? No, he did too, Kit Harris. Yeah, trumpet, yeah. Me and Louie and George used to play with Kit Harris. He's a good trampone player, Louie Nelson did.
Who was the main player?
I thought you were talking about the other Louie Nelson, flying up players, saxophone.
Who else was there?
See, there's a dine time somewhere. The youth, I don't know if it is, yes, you know. See, who else was in the band?
With Kit Harris.
With Kit Harris. Well, I think me, Louie, George, and I played a girlfriend.
On piano?
No, I mean Kit Harris' girlfriend, you know.
She played piano?

Yeah, playing piano with a thing, you know. And then they had big George Williams with us, you know. You know him, George Williams? Played drums. Played drums? Yeah, he was playing with I-tay, you know, about a couple of weeks ago.
Did he have a bass player?

Have a bass player? A bass player, yeah. He named, uh, Richard, Richard, uh, Green, something. Richard Green, something, the bass player. Richard McLean, yeah, that's him, McLean. Oh, Richard McLean, yeah. I know him. Yeah, yeah. He played with I-tay, Viet. I think. He used to play guitar. He got a son, he really can play guitar. Fafu. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Fafu is his name, yeah. Yeah, he really played. I don't know if they, yeah, I've been sick so long, I don't get around him no more, you know. Did you have a way with Franky Dusen? Franky Dusen? Played in his band, here's another one, Cook. Oh! Oh, Franky, come to your house and say, uh, if you come for me, he says, Clancy? And my niece said, no, he's not there. He said, well, he sent me up there, told me to get two dollars, and, uh, he said, uh, for me to meet him down, then he'd pay back, say, the next day, when, you know, British come home. And we ain't never seen a Franky Dusen. We see him. He never did pay his back to him, you know. No. So when I joined his band, I stayed with him about two weeks, and I quit him, you know. The mother-father tried to make him creep, but actually he got crooked, nobody wouldn't bother with him no more. No.
